findings.title: The 'still unsettled at 99 ms' assertion is vacuous: the test does not pin the 100 ms budget, and the PR body says it does
findings.evidence: scripts/ovd419-acquisition-preparation.test.mjs:590-591 runs `await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(99); expect(settled).toBe(false);`. After the bounded receipt open rejects, persist cannot settle until the real directory-handle closes finish (closeOwnedHandle, reader :114, `Promise.resolve().then(() => handle.close())`, which is real libuv I/O). advanceTimersByTimeAsync only flushes microtasks, so `settled` is always false at that point, even if the budget timer already fired. I ran production mutants on a scratch copy of scripts/ovd419-synthetic-acquisition-reader.mjs, :84 changed to `Math.min(remaining, 30000) - 1` (99 ms budget) and then `- 90` (10 ms budget), with `npx vitest run scripts/ovd419-acquisition-preparation.test.mjs -t "fails closed without cleanup when a filesystem operation never settles"`. The unchanged head test PASSED 1/1 with the 99 ms budget and 3/3 with the 10 ms budget (`Tests  1 passed | 43 skipped (44)`). Only the upper bound is pinned: a budget that never fires would hang at `await outcome`. The PR body ('Acceptance criteria addressed', item 3) lists 'still unsettled at 99 ms, rejected with `cleanup_unproved` at 100 ms' as one of the added exact counts. The test does not check that. The issue's four criteria are otherwise met (see checks_run), so this is one vacuous assertion and an overstated claim, not a vacuous test.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the 99 ms check look at the race, not at persist settling. Option 1 (deterministic): wrap the root and child directory handles in the existing open mock (paths whose basename is the fixture root or starts with `ovd419-acquisition-`) with a close spy, as the 'refuses settlement when directory close crosses the original deadline' test does. Then assert zero closes after `advanceTimersByTimeAsync(99)` and the expected closes after the final 1 ms. The catch path reaches handle.close() through microtasks only, so a timer that fired early shows up at once. Option 2: drain real I/O (setImmediate is not faked) before `expect(settled).toBe(false)`. I tried 200 setImmediate turns on a scratch copy: it caught the 10 ms mutant 3/3 but the 99 ms mutant only 2/3, so prefer option 1. If neither is wanted, remove the 99 ms assertion and the 'still unsettled at 99 ms' claim from the PR body.
